stem:
Omar looks at the diagram of triangle $DEF$. Segment $EH$ meets side $DF$ at $H$, and the right-angle mark at $H$ is shown. Point $M$ is the midpoint of $DF$.

Which claim correctly names $EH$?

options.text: $EH$ is an altitude from $E$ to base $DF$, because it is perpendicular to $DF$.
Call $EH$ an altitude even when $EH$ need not be perpendicular to $DF$.
Say the same segment also settles the area formula for every triangle, with no further check.
Name $EH$ an altitude because $M$ is labelled on $DF$, using the midpoint mark alone.

teacher.key_rationale: An altitude from $E$ to $DF$ is the perpendicular segment from $E$ to that side, so $EH$ with the right-angle mark is the altitude. Dropping perpendicularity, stretching into a general area rule, or using only the midpoint label all miss that hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as triangle DEF with altitude EH to DF (right angle at H) and midpoint M on DF.
